lessons.what: Changes who can read, write or run a file.
lessons.when: You wrote a script but Linux says 'Permission denied'. Make it runnable.
lessons.tip: Numbers: r=4 w=2 x=1. So 7 = rwx, 6 = rw-, 4 = r--.

lessons.what: Changes which user (and group) owns a file.
lessons.when: You created files using sudo and now root owns them. Take them back.
lessons.tip: user:group changes both at once. -R for folders.

lessons.what: Changes only the group that owns a file.
lessons.when: Sharing a project folder with your team's group.
lessons.tip: Groups let several users share access.

lessons.man: Display or set file mode mask.
lessons.what: Sets the default permissions for every new file you create.
lessons.when: You want new files to be private by default.
lessons.tip: umask removes permissions. 077 = only you.

lessons.man: print real and effective user and group IDs
lessons.what: Shows your user ID and every group you belong to.
lessons.when: 'Permission denied' on a shared folder. Are you even in that group?
lessons.tip: uid 0 is always root.

quiz.q: With umask 077, new files can be read by...
quiz.why: 077 removes all access for group and others.

quiz.q: Which uid always belongs to root?

lessons.man: execute a command as another user
lessons.what: Runs a single command with admin (root) powers.
lessons.when: Installing software or changing system files. With great power...
lessons.tip: sudo !! re-runs your last command with sudo.

lessons.man: run a command with substitute user and group ID
lessons.what: Switches you to another user account in the terminal.
lessons.when: Testing how things look from another user's account.
lessons.tip: The - gives you that user's full login environment.

lessons.what: Changes your password.
lessons.when: Your password is 'password123'. Please. Change it.
lessons.tip: Nothing appears while typing. That's normal.

lessons.man: print the groups a user is in
lessons.what: Lists the groups you (or another user) belong to.
lessons.when: Checking if you were added to the 'docker' or 'sudo' group.
lessons.tip: New group added? Log out and in to see it.

lessons.what: Shows who is logged into this computer right now.
lessons.when: On a shared lab server: is anyone else using it?
lessons.tip: who am i shows just your own session.

quiz.q: What does the - in su - friend do?
quiz.why: It loads that user's login settings.

quiz.q: Typing a password in passwd shows...

lessons.man: report a snapshot of the current processes.
lessons.what: Lists running programs (processes) with their IDs.
lessons.when: Is that program still running in the background?
lessons.tip: 2nd column = PID, the process's ID number.

lessons.what: Live dashboard of what's using your CPU and memory.
lessons.when: Fan going crazy, laptop is lagging. Who's the culprit?
lessons.tip: Inside top: P sorts by CPU, M by memory, q quits.

lessons.man: send a signal to a process
lessons.what: Sends a signal to a process, usually to stop it.
lessons.when: A program froze and won't close. Time to step in.
lessons.tip: Plain kill asks politely. -9 forces it. Use -9 last.

lessons.man: look up or signal processes based on name and other attributes
lessons.what: Stops processes by name instead of by number.
lessons.when: You don't know the PID, you just know Firefox is frozen.
lessons.tip: -u stops every process of that user.

lessons.man: look up or signal processes based on name and other attributes
lessons.what: Finds the PIDs of processes by name.
lessons.when: Quick check: is my server script still running?
lessons.tip: -l shows names too. pgrep + pkill are a pair.

quiz.q: In ps aux output, the PID is...
Inside top, which key sorts by memory?

lessons.what: Lists programs you started from this terminal that are paused or in the background.
lessons.when: You paused a few things with Ctrl+Z and lost track of them.
lessons.tip: Ctrl + Z pauses the current program.

lessons.what: Resumes a paused job and lets it run in the background.
lessons.when: A long download is hogging your terminal. Push it to the background.
lessons.tip: Adding & at the end starts a job in background directly.

lessons.what: Brings a background or paused job back to the front.
lessons.when: You paused your editor to check something. Now get back to it.
lessons.tip: %1, %2... pick which job.

lessons.man: run a command immune to hangups, with output to a non-tty
lessons.what: Keeps a program running even after you close the terminal.
lessons.when: Starting a long task, then closing your laptop lid and going to class.
lessons.tip: Output goes to nohup.out by default.

lessons.man: delay for a specified amount of time
lessons.what: Waits for a set time, then continues.
lessons.when: In scripts: 'wait 5 seconds, then try again'.
lessons.tip: Units: s seconds, m minutes, h hours.

quiz.q: Ctrl + Z does what to a running program?

options: Resumes a job in the background

quiz.q: nohup keeps a command running after...

lessons.what: Shows how much disk space is used and free.
lessons.when: 'Disk full' error. Let's see how bad it is.
example: Filesystem  Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
lessons.tip: -h = human-readable (G, M) sizes.

lessons.what: Shows how much space files and folders take.
lessons.when: Disk is full. Which folder is the space monster?
lessons.tip: -s summary, -h human sizes. Pair with sort -h.

lessons.man: Display amount of free and used memory in the system
lessons.what: Shows how much RAM is used and available.
lessons.when: Too many Chrome tabs? Check if you're out of memory.
lessons.tip: Look at 'available', not 'free'.

lessons.what: Lists your disks, USB drives and their partitions as a tree.
lessons.when: You plugged in a pendrive. What name did Linux give it?
lessons.tip: sdb here is the new pendrive.

lessons.what: Attaches a disk or pendrive to a folder so you can open its files.
lessons.when: Your pendrive shows up in lsblk but you can't open it yet.
lessons.tip: Linux treats drives as folders. Mounting = plugging in.

quiz.q: Best combo to find the biggest folders?
In free -h, which column matters most?

options: Attaches a drive to a folder
quiz.why: It makes the drive's files accessible.
